description: DGX Spark (GB10) whose GPU failed GSP initialisation at boot (spec section 10 variant gb10-gsp-fail, strings from spec 3.2 / S12). Same machine, DGX OS and packages as gb10.json, but every nvidia-smi invocation prints 'No devices were found' (spec 3.2) and dmesg carries the Xid 119 GSP RPC timeout, the ksec2PrepareBootCommands_GB20B SEC2 secure-boot timeout, 'RmInitAdapter: Cannot initialize GSP firmware RM' and 'RmInitAdapter failed! (0x62:0x65:2028)' (all spec 3.2). lspci still lists [10de:2e12] at 000f:01:00.0 (spec 3.1 row 5) and lsmod still shows the nvidia modules loaded. The OTA checker reports failed: ["driver"] (spec 3.2). Expected (spec 10): dgx-spark-gsp-init-failure CRIT; forbidden: no-nvidia-gpu (spec 5.1 also suppresses driver-not-detected). lspci_lines and other_netdevs carry the same omissions as gb10.json (no PCIe root ports, no mgmt-NIC / Wi-Fi PCI ids: spec 2.1 names only the drivers). PLACEHOLDERS: the nvidia-smi exit code for 'No devices were found' (6 here) is not in the spec (the collectors only test for non-zero), and, as in gb10.json, the DGX_SWBUILD_DATE / DGX_SWBUILD_VERSION / DGX_COMMIT_ID / DGX_OTA_DATE values, the fastos-release VERSION and the BIOS release date are inherited from the draft scenario (the spec gives only the key list). INTEGRATION ADDITIONS (2026-09-02, after WP1-WP5 merged): journal_boots / journal_units / hostname feed the journalctl shim (previous boot ends with the systemd 255 shutdown lines 'Shutting down.', 'systemd-shutdown', 'Journal stopped'; these are systemd behaviour, not hardware facts, and the boot id / timestamps are placeholders); ldconfig_libs lists the driver libraries the collectors look up (libcuda.so.1, libnvidia-ml.so.1 under the Ubuntu arm64 multiarch dir, the same path linux.go probes; whether a CUDA toolkit is preinstalled is unconfirmed, so no libcudart entry); netplan persists the cage-0 addresses with mtu 9000 (spec 9 'MTU 9000 on every node'; the file name 50-cx7.yaml is a placeholder); cx7_hotplug_enabled creates /etc/nvidia/cx7-hotplug-enabled (spec 9 lists the file; whether a stock unit ships it is unconfirmed, the analyzer only echoes its presence); docker writes /etc/docker/daemon.json with the nvidia runtime plus features.cdi and /etc/cdi/nvidia.yaml (the toolkit's documented 'nvidia-ctk runtime configure' / 'nvidia-ctk cdi generate' result; whether DGX OS enables CDI by default is unconfirmed); apt_sources carries NVIDIA's documented nvidia-container-toolkit.list line (S44 checks its first line). gb10-clock-cap.service was removed from systemd_units: it is a community add-on (S48), a stock unit has no such unit file, and the collector now asks systemctl show -p LoadState so a listed-but-inactive unit would read as installed.
